stem: For a school science activity, Meena tests a spoonful of crushed groundnuts (peanuts) from her kitchen. The Biuret test turns purple and the food also leaves a greasy translucent patch on paper. What do these two results together show?

options.text: Groundnuts contain only proteins and no other nutrient.
One food item can contain more than one nutrient, since groundnuts show both proteins and fats.
The tests cancel each other, so groundnuts contain neither proteins nor fats.
Groundnuts contain only fats because the paper test is stronger than the Biuret test.

teacher.key_rationale: A purple Biuret result indicates protein and a translucent greasy patch on paper indicates fat; two positive tests on one food item show it contains more than one nutrient. Option B alone states this; A and D wrongly claim a single nutrient and C wrongly treats one positive test as cancelling the other.
